/-!
# Conjecture 20.76
by L. Pyber
*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
!-/

@[expose] public section
namespace Kourovka.«20.76»
/--
Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group and assume that all abelian normal subgroups of $G$
have order at most $p^k$. Is it true that every abelian subgroup of $G$ has order at most
$p^{2k}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka_20_76 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᵉ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (hg : IsPGroup p G) (_ : Finite G) (k : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ H: Subgroup G, H.Normal ∧ IsMulCommutative H → Nat.card H ≤ p ^ k),
    (∀ H : Subgroup G, IsMulCommutative H → Nat.card H ≤ p ^ (2 * k)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«20.76»

review.notes: The sole declaration, Kourovka.«20.76».kourovka_20_76, faithfully states Pyber’s question. The quantifiers, normal-and-abelian hypothesis, arbitrary abelian subgroup conclusion, and bounds p^k and p^(2*k) agree with the source. The answer slot has the correct scope and polarity. Lean checks confirmed the finite-cardinality characterization of IsPGroup, inherited subgroup commutativity, and positive finite subgroup cardinalities. Boundary tests covered the trivial group, a nontrivial example at p=2, and k=0; the latter is harmless because a nontrivial finite p-group has a nontrivial abelian normal center. All experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiled without errors. The latest source, v46, retains Problem 20.76 without a recorded solution, consistent with research open.
